Daily Brief

The day's most significant developments center on the ongoing US-Iran conflict, European wildfires, and a deadly attack in Berlin. After nearly two weeks of nightly US bombardments on Iran, operations have paused, with reports suggesting dwindling munitions stockpiles may be constraining Washington's options [France 24, ABC Australia, The Hindu]. Diplomatic efforts continue, with an Omani delegation in Tehran for talks on the Strait of Hormuz. In Europe, devastating wildfires have displaced over 330,000 people across France and Spain, with France mobilizing military assets including an A400M cargo plane to combat blazes threatening Bordeaux [BBC, RFI, Globe and Mail]. The Tour de France's final stage was shortened to redeploy security personnel. In Berlin, a van attack on Pride celebrations killed one person and injured at least 16 others; police have identified a 21-year-old suspect with alleged ties to Islamist groups and warned he may be armed [France 24, Le Monde, Financial Times]. Meanwhile, Russian ballistic missile strikes on a drone exhibition near Kyiv killed at least 10 people and injured around 100 [BBC], and India's Education Minister resigned following weeks of youth-led protests over examination irregularities [BBC].
